all_quotes.quote: CO$^+$ is responsible for producing at most a few percent of the HCO$^+$ that recombines with ambient thermal electrons to form CO in diffuse molecular gas.
A baseline cosmic-ray and UV-driven thermal chemical model overproduced HOC$^+$ by a factor two, but by as much as a factor six
such heavily over-pressured gas is more properly considered in the context of a turbulent dissipation chemistry
We chose to search for the $N=2\rightarrow1$ transitions because the frequencies of this first excited transition near 236 GHz are easily accessible from ground-based radio observatories
that were known to have high intervening column densities of Galactic neutral gas detected in molecular absorption
Absorption spectroscopy represents the best method to probe the molecular content of diffuse clouds because the molecular excitation is weak at the low densities

The CO$^+$ ground state rotational transitions at 117.7 GHz and 118.1 GHz are close to a strong atmospheric line from molecular oxygen at 118.75 GHz, rendering their observation from the ground very difficult.
